claims.text: The alloy system is Ti65(AlCrNbV)35-xZrx with Zr varied from 3 to 10 wt.%.
The proposed processing route uses approximately 50% hot rolling, 70% cold rolling, and rapid annealing near 850°C at about 15 K/s.
Optimized Zr alloying combined with the proposed thermomechanical treatment produces uniform lattice distortion.
Optimized Zr alloying combined with the proposed thermomechanical treatment produces refined, homogeneous grains.
Zr induces lattice distortion because of its large atomic-radius difference from the other alloying elements.
Zr-induced lattice distortion provides solid-solution strengthening.
Zr additions promote grain refinement in this alloy system.
Fine, uniformly distributed grains enhance ductility through grain-boundary toughening.
Fine, uniformly distributed grains positively tune Young's modulus.
The combination of lattice distortion and controlled grain size mitigates crack propagation.
The processed alloy will have yield strength exceeding 1200 MPa.
The processed alloy will have plastic strain capacity above 15%.
The processed alloy will have enhanced Young's modulus relative to the state of the art.
The processed alloy will have greater fracture resistance than alloys made without optimized Zr additions.
The initial alloy has yield strength below 1200 MPa.
The initial alloy has plastic strain below 15%.
Alloys processed without targeted Zr optimization typically possess coarse to moderately refined grains.
Conventionally processed Ti65(AlCrNbV)35 alloys have lower yield strength and ductility than the proposed alloy.
Loss of microstructural uniformity or abnormal grain growth can eliminate the proposed property improvements and restore the strength-ductility trade-off.
Zr content and processing fluctuations may produce nonlinear changes in mechanical properties.

contradictions.description: The formula Ti65(AlCrNbV)35-xZrx is normalized like an atomic-percent composition, but the intervention defines x as wt.%. Thus the composition variable and its units are internally inconsistent.

The prediction specifies total plastic strain above 15%, whereas the falsification rule refers to 'plastic strain improvements under 15%,' which implies a 15-percentage-point improvement rather than a 15% final strain.
